assignment:
Your principal is considering changing school policy so that students may not participate in sports or other activities unless they have at least a grade B average. Many students have a grade C average. 
She would like to hear the students' views on this possible policy change. Write a letter to your principal arguing for or against requiring at least a grade B average to participate in sports or other activities. Be sure to support your arguments with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I heard you are thinking about changing the rule so that students need a B average to play sports or be in other activities. I understand why you would want that, since school is supposed to come first. But I think this rule would hurt way more kids than it would help, so I am asking you to please keep it at a C.

First of all, a C is a passing grade. If you have a C average you are doing what the school asks, even if it isn't great. A lot of us study really hard and still get C's, especially in hard classes like algebra and science. If you take away the team or band from those kids, your basically punishing them for trying.

Another reason is that activities are the reason some kids even try in class. My friend is on the soccer team and he does his homework on the bus because the coach checks grades every Friday. If he got kicked off the team he would not start studying more. He would just go home and play video games and his grades would get even worse.

Also, activities teach you things you don't learn in class. You learn to show up on time and work with people you didn't pick. You learn how to lose and not quit. The kids who have trouble in class probably need that more then anybody.

One more thing is that a lot of students have a C average, so the teams and clubs would get a lot smaller. Some of them might not even have enough people to keep going.

I think a better idea would be to keep the C rule and add tutoring for kids who are close to failing. That way grades could go up without taking away the thing that makes us want to come to school in the first place.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the idea to make students have a B average to be in sports and other activities. I get why people want it, since school comes first. I still think the rule should stay at a C.

First, a C is passing. A kid with a C average is doing what the school asks. A lot of us study every night and that is where we end up, mostly in classes like algebra or science. The grade is only a C, but the work behind it is hard and honest.

Second, activities are what keep some kids going in class. My friend plays soccer and he does his homework on the bus, because the coach checks grades every Friday. He says math is boring, but he would hate to miss a game, so he does it. If you took soccer away, he would go home and sit on his phone.

Third, you learn things on a team that you do not get in a classroom. You have to show up on time. You have to work with people you did not pick. You have to finish the season even when the scores go the other way.

Also, so many students have a C that the teams and clubs would get small. Some of them would not have enough people to keep going. That is not fair to the kids who do have a B, because they would lose their team too.

I think there is another plan. Keep the C rule, and add tutoring after school for students whose grades are low. Coaches could let players leave practice to go. It would take time and it might not fix every grade, but kids would still have a reason to come to school. Please think about it before you change the rule.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
